sentences.text: FACTS OF THE CASE 1.
Briefly stated, the facts of the petition are that on 15.01.2024, at about 03:00 p.m., one minor girl namely Pragya Bodh (injured) was going to park alongwith her mother namely Anita.

It has been alleged that when they reached near gate no. 02 of Dayanand Vihar, within the jurisdiction of PS Anand Vihar Delhi, a Bullet (make and model Royal Enfield), bearing registration no. UP16CW7450 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle), came at a very high speed and hit her with a great force.

It has been further alleged that the offending vehicle was being driven by its driver i.e.
respondent no. 1 (R1) herein, at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner without taking due caution at the time of the accident.
Allegedly, the above-said minor girl fell down on the road after being hit by the offending vehicle and she sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner/injured was thereon taken to ESI Indira Gandhi Hospital.
An FIR in this regard was also registered at PS Anand Vihar, Delhi, vide FIR no. 55/24, for the offences u/s 279/337 IPC.

The present DAR petition thereafter came to be filed in due course on 07.05.2024.
WS / Reply of Respondents 2.

The respondents no. 1 & 2, being the driver & owner of the offending vehicle respectively, filed their joint reply/ written statement to the DAR, wherein it has been contended that the accident took place due to sole negligence of the Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.09.06 16:20:54 +0530 injured herself and that the respondents have been falsely implicated in the present case.

Nevertheless, it has been stated that the offending vehicle was duly insured with the Magma HDI General Insurance Company i.e. R3 herein, vide policy no. P0022000100/4113/706827, with its validity from 28.04.2021 to 27.04.2026, in the name of Respondent no. 02 and that its driver ie.
R1, was having a valid DL at the time of the accident.
The respondent no. 01 and 02 denied all the allegations against them and prayed for the dismissal of the DAR petition.

3. Respondent no. 3 i.e. Magma HDI General Insurance Company, filed its separate detailed written statement, wherein it has been admitted that the offending vehicle was duly insured with the company vide insurance policy no. P0022000100/4113/706827, with its validity from 28.04.2021 to 27.04.2026.
However, the R3 denied all the averments of the DAR petition and prayed for its dismissal.

Issue wise findings Issue no.1

Whether petitioner suffered injuries during the accident caused by rash and negligence driving of respondent no. 01 being driver of vehicle no. UP16CW7450 on 15.01.2024 at about 03:00 pm in front of Gate no. 02, Dayanand Vihar, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS Anand Vihar, Delhi ?

10.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530,

sentences.text: The PW1 has specifically stated during her cross-examination that her daughter i.e. victim in the present case, was walking ahead of her on the road at the time of the accident and that the accident took place due to rash and negligent act of R1.

The claim put forth by the petitioner and the contentions regarding the rash and negligent act of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the time of the accident are duly corroborated by the findings of the IO/police as mentioned in the site plan, mechanical inspection report, seizure memo, Charge sheet along with other documents pertaining to criminal case in respect of the incident in question brought on record as Ex. PW1/4 and no ground has been made out by the respondents to disbelieve the same.

The testimony of PW1 for the petitioner has remained consistent and no doubt has been raised by the respondents to disbelieve the same.
12.

The respondent no.1 i.e. driver, respondent no. 02 i.e. owner of the Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.09.06 16:21:17 +0530 offending vehicle and respondent no. 3 i.e. Insurance Company, have neither impeached the testimony of PW-1 nor they have led any material evidence to substantiate their claim that the accident was caused due to fault of the petitioner or that they have been falsely implicated in the present case.

The evidence of the star witness in this case i.e. PW-1 on the aspect of rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 while driving the offending vehicle at the time of the accident,
has remained unimpeached and her testimony has to be accepted on its face value itself.

13. The very fact that R-1 has already been specifically arrayed as an accused in case 360/23, u/s 279/337/338 IPC, PS Shahdara, Delhi, is also a strong circumstance to support the above said testimony of PW-1 on these issues.
The copies of FIR, Site plan, seizure memos, mechanical inspection, notice u/s 133 MV Act and charge sheet u/s 173 Cr.P.C also corroborate the oral testimony of PW1.

Furthermore, the position of law in this regard has been made clear in the case of "National Insurance Co., Vs Puspha Rana", 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, wherein it has been held that filing of Chargesheet is sufficient proof of the negligence and involvement of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: 5 14. In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that the offending vehicle was being driven by R-1 indeed at the time of incident and that the injuries have been caused to the petitioner on account of the incident in question itself.

15. Having ruled so, this Tribunal now proceeds to assess the wrongful act, neglect or default of R-1,
if any, in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Admittedly, R-1 has not explained the circumstances under which his vehicle (i.e. the offending vehicle ) hit the petitioner/injured with a great force.

In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner or any other such person, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

In view of the above discussion, this tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time leading to the injuries to petitioner Pragya.
16. In view of the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, no dispute is left regarding the injuries to the petitioner Pragya in the above accident.
17. In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the injured Pragya suffered injuries on account of neglect and default of R1 while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

The issue at hand is thus decided against Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.09.06 16:21:29 +0530 the respondents and in favour of the petitioner.
Issue no. (ii) Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

OPP. 
18.

On the basis of findings upon issue no. (i), it is clear that the incident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and injuries had been caused to the petitioner in the incident.
Hence, petitioner is entitled to compensation in this case.
19. The issue at hand is accordingly decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
LIABILITY 20.
Now the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Herein, it is pertinent to note that the respondent no. 3 i.e. Insurance Company has specifically admitted in its written statement that the offending vehicle bearing registration no.
UP16CW7450 was duly insured at the time of accident with respondent no. 3 vide policy no.
P0022000100/4113/706827, with its validity from 28.04.2021 to 27.04.2026.
Furthermore, the respondent no. 03 has failed to bring on record or to prove any breach of the terms or conditions of the said insurance policy by the respondents no.01 and 02 in any manner.

Admittedly, R-1 has not explained the circumstances under which his vehicle (i.e. the offending vehicle ) hit the petitioner/injured with a great force.
In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner or any other such person, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion, this tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time leading to the injuries to petitioner Pragya.
On the basis of findings upon issue no. (i), it is clear that the incident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and injuries had been caused to the petitioner in the incident.
Hence, petitioner is entitled to compensation in this case.
Furthermore, the respondent no. 03 has failed to bring on record or to prove any breach of the terms or conditions of the said insurance policy by the respondents no.01 and 02 in any manner.
Hence, on the basis of entire above stated facts and circumstances and discussion of evidence,
this Tribunal is of the opinion that respondent no. 3 i.e. insurance company is liable to pay the entire compensation to the petitioner on Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
2025.09.06 16:21:35 +0530 behalf of respondents no. 1 and 2, without any recovery rights against the respondent no. 01 and 02.
